decision.governing_rule: rule 3: deep-but-narrow technical work caps at L5 despite broad scope of impact
decision.reasoning: The advocate's argument rests almost entirely on Nyx's own leveling principle ("a person who has gone deep enough in one area... belongs at the top of the ladder for that reason alone") and Nyx's Principal/Distinguished MTS anchors. That is inadmissible as a governing framework here -- per section 7, the advocate may cite Nyx's document only as evidence about the employee's described scope, not as a rule this arbiter weighs against Meridian's framework. Stripped of that borrowed rule, the advocate cites no new scope evidence beyond what the original mapping already captured and rated: the mandatory, cross-product-line sign-off gate is already reflected in the scope_of_impact (L6) and ownership_scope (L5) ratings. The dispositive facts remain undisputed: the employee has never worked outside this one methodology area, and there is no external recognition (no patents, no publications). Under this framework, rule 3 is explicit and unambiguous -- deep-but-narrow technical work caps at L5 regardless of how broad the scope of impact of that narrow work becomes, and technical_depth_breadth and influence both independently land at L5. Rule 4 independently forecloses L6/L7 treatment on external-recognition grounds for anything above L6, and even setting that aside, rule 3 alone controls. That said, this is precisely the shape of case section 7 contemplates for red-circling: the scope-of-impact evidence (mandatory company-wide sign-off gate across NX-400/NX-500) genuinely would support L6 under the ordinary scope-of-impact anchor and would even be the rule-1 tiebreaker in an unconstrained split -- it is rule 3's deep-but-narrow cap, specifically, that holds the level down despite that scope evidence. The original mapping itself flagged this tension (confidence 0.6, scope pointing to L6). This is a genuinely contested, merit-bearing case, not a routine call, so red-circling rather than a flat upheld is the correct disposition: level stays at L5, with pay protection to be handled downstream by the retention/comp mechanism.</reasoning>
